proof_summary: Using the prime factorization formula for $v_2(\varphi(m))$, the proof bounds each odd prime factor $p$ in terms of $c=v_2(p-1)$: equality in $p\ge 2^c+1$ forces a Fermat prime, while otherwise $p\ge 3\cdot2^c+1$. Product and geometric-sum bounds then show that any admissible $m<2^{2^{33}+1}$ must equal $F_{33}$ and make it prime; since both $2^{2^{33}+1}$ and, when prime, $F_{33}$ are admissible, the two cases follow by minimality.
